rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-seven builder trees go (a row of queen palms, corals and torrey pines every 6 m along the back fences, fan and queen palms 3 m from the house fronts, others in the yards); seven come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the picnic table, the grill and the chair, on the open lot corner, in two back yards, and one on the old back fence row.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 13 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the big open lot corner, 35 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the back yard with the adirondack chair and the gas grill: a magnolia over both
the north-west back yard, 8.7 m from the house: the yard's tree
the north back yard, 8 m from the house, 54 m from the next
the west back fence row: the row's one tree (it had one every 6-10 m)
